No, there's not, but it should be unnecessary. They should be stopped only once the main process receives and returns all batches. What arguments did you pass in to the DataLoader constructor (other than the dataset)?

```Python
    @staticmethod
    def collate_fn(batch):
        org_audio_len_lst, audio_lst, spec_linear_lst, spec_mel_lst, speaker_class_lst, sample_info_lst = zip(*batch)
        audio_arr = np.stack(audio_lst,0).astype('float32')
        spec_linear_arr = np.stack(spec_linear_lst, 0).astype('float32')
        spec_mel_arr = np.stack(spec_mel_lst, 0).astype('float32')

        audio_arr = torch.from_numpy(audio_arr)    
        spec_linear_arr = torch.from_numpy(spec_linear_arr)
        spec_mel_arr = torch.from_numpy(spec_mel_arr)
        speaker_class_tensor = torch.LongTensor(speaker_class_lst)
        return {'audio': audio_arr, 'spec_linear': spec_linear_arr, 'spec_mel': spec_mel_arr,
                'speaker_class': speaker_class_tensor}

```

That's because numpy arrays are pickled and unpickled instead of using shared memory. There are probably very tight limits on the shared memory size in your systems, or the workers quit in a weird way. Does it happen at the end of an epoch?

I'm running into an issue when trying to predict with the dn models.  From what I've researched it seems maybe related to this issue https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/973 from the pytorch forums and the workaround there was setting the number of workers to 0.  If anybody else has encountered this or knows how to set the number of workers to 0, I tried setting num_workers on ImageClassifierData to 0, but that didn't solve the issue for me.  I don't know if there is anything that can be done on the fastai side since it appears to be a pytorch problem, but I figured it's at least worth documenting and if anybody has any ideas they can look into it.

body: Increasing the `ulimit` solved the issue.  Details (https://github.com/fastai/fastai/issues/23).  When using Docker, the `ulimit` is set very high so you may never see the issue, but Ubuntu instance by default had 1024 (file descriptor limit).  Increasing it to 2048 or 4096 or higher solves the issue.  I don't know why that many file descriptors are required, but glad that it had a simple fix.
If the core devs want to see the error, just reduce the `ulimit` to 1024 and run the code of @kamo-naoyuki above and you might see the same problem.

This does seem to be an issue in pytorch as best as we can tell - FDs aren't being released when they should be. As @sampathweb mentioned, it's reproducible using the above code. The workaround for now is:

```
import resource
rlimit = resource.getrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE)
resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE, (2048, rlimit[1]))
```
(You may need to set 2048 to a higher number.)
